artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied most specifications of a complaint filed by TE Herron and others against Central Indiana Presbytery's investigative and suspension procedures, but sustained the complaint on the point that Presbytery improperly denied Herron access to Presbytery minutes while under process. The decision includes extensive discussion of pre-trial BCO 43-1 complaints ('interlocutory appeals') and the proper scope of BCO 31-10 administrative suspensions.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Bachmann appealed Nashville Presbytery's decision to amend its judicial commission's recommended censure of admonition to indefinite suspension; the SJC sustained the appeal, finding NP violated BCO 15-3 by dividing the question and amending the JC's judgment, and rendered the decision that should have been rendered by restoring the JC's censure of admonition.

artifacts.title: Complaint TE Anthony Dallison v. Northern Florida Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 156 Objection by TE Frank Smith 30-40, p. 204 Amendment to Objection 30-65, p. 342
artifacts.synopsis: TE Anthony Dallison appealed his deposition from the office of Teaching Elder by North Florida Presbytery, arguing that presbytery lacked authority to increase his censure from indefinite suspension to deposition without conducting a new trial. The SJC affirmed presbytery's decision, holding that where a teaching elder has confessed guilt under BCO 38-1, presbytery may impose additional censure based on evidence of impenitence without initiating new charges, and such disciplinary discretion is within presbytery's constitutional authority.

artifacts.disposition: in conflict; Adopted by the CCB

matches.evidence: CCB found in conflict an overture to amend BCO 25-2 mandating annual congregational meetings and specific financial reporting standards.
The CCB determined that amending BCO 36 to mandate public excommunication would create a conflict with current BCO provisions, though the overture was adopted.
